# Agatha Sowerby

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c9 P0](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0000), [v1 c9 P16](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0016), [v1 c9 P31](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0031)</sub>

## Appearance

Mrs. Agatha Sowerby is a stout, heavy woman weighing two hundred pounds whose movement is characterized by a perpetual waddle. She sits for long hours by her kitchen window watching the main thoroughfare. Her feet carry her heavy weight with difficulty.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c9 P31](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0031), [v1 c38 P30](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0030), [v1 c38 P31](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0031)_

## Personality

Mrs. Sowerby is a industrious, candid, and meddlesome busybody who speaks her mind freely without fear or partiality. She takes great pleasure in being consulted for advice, boasting of her achievements, and managing the affairs of others alongside her own. While she can be critical, judgmental, and skeptical of higher education for women, she also possesses a kind heart and sincere Christian piety. She is a passionate partisan in politics and prides herself on her foresight.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c9 P45](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0045), [v1 c10 P1](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0001), [v1 c10 P33](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0033), [v1 c15 P84](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0084), [v1 c15 P89](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0089), [v1 c16 P26](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0026), [v1 c18 P1](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0001), [v1 c21 P5](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0005), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 c31 P7](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0007), [v1 c36 P32](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0032), [v1 c38 P31](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0031)_

## History

Residing at Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley with her husband Thomas, Mrs. Agatha Sowerby spent her days keeping diligent watch over the neighborhood thoroughfare while managing various church organizations. When Nell Harcourt first arrived at Grey Shutters, Mrs. Sowerby visited after recovering from influenza and made sharp remarks about Nell's plain appearance and red hair, provoking a passionate outburst from the young girl. Though initially offended, she forgave Nell after receiving a humbled apology. Over the following years, she offered advice to Thirza and Obed Abernethy regarding Nell's upbringing, made dresses for Nell, and attended church and community events, including winning first prize for butter and cheese at an exhibition. Although she expressed doubts about Nell's character and opposed women's higher education, she eventually praised Nell's growth and personal development while remaining pleased when Nell gave up plans to attend college.
